description: TACO is a litter-image dataset and associated preparation code published by Pedro Proença and Pedro Simões. Images show waste in woods, roads and beaches, with manually segmented objects and a hierarchical class taxonomy. Annotations use COCO-style structures, and the repository supplies inspection, download and dataset-splitting scripts. Coverage is a collection of photographed scenes, not a representative geographic survey; a common acquisition period is not stated. The version 1.0 dataset is publicly archived on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0, verified through DataCite rights metadata, while repository software uses MIT. A limitation is strong class imbalance: the authors recommend merging or excluding sparsely annotated classes. The unofficial annotation stream is explicitly unreviewed and may contain poor labels. TACO can calibrate waste-detection components in simulations of collection or sorting services, complementing the system-level waste model SwolfPy (model-swolfpy). The repository cites its 2020 dataset paper and provides a Mask R-CNN workflow. A rejected candidate concerns a later YOLO paper, not this original resource. No images or trained weights were downloaded.
